text: Attempt 5: a high-value city. Homes touch shops, factories are buffered by shops and kept at the south edge, parks in every home segment, dense homes by the lakes, power plant on the river strip away from homes.

Day one: $10,000 bond, taxes homes 6% / shops 5% / factories 4%. Block 1: dense homes y21-26, shops y28-33, homes y35-40, shops y42-47, factories y49-54; 32 small parks; coal plant on the river strip; 12 wired pumps; fire station.
Joined pumps to the pipe main (1-tile gap at x=73); 68 buildings had no water
Replaced park columns with power lines: parks blocked power from reaching the home zones, so homes could not grow
7 more pumps x=72 y34-40 (water spare hit 0%)
New factory strip y57-61 x78-100 with road y=62: factory demand at max, 14% unemployed, shops overbuilt
Turned on legal gambling and parking fines (+$38/yr). Tax income only $350/yr vs $540 costs
Loan #2 ($10k) and second coal plant x64-67 y61-64: power spare was 7%, which stalled factory growth
